records.name: Philly Roller Derby
records.summary: A roller derby league run by its skaters, with adult travel teams, a league skater group, and a juniors program. It also needs officials, support crew, and volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Skate through the new skater program, help as an official or on the support crew, or volunteer.

schedule.text: An eight week adult new skater bootcamp starts on a Sunday afternoon. Officiating training happens at Wednesday night scrimmages.

cost.text: Volunteering and non-skating officiating cost nothing. The eight week adult bootcamp is $60, paid at registration and not refundable. Skating officials buy their own gear and pay for annual insurance.

requirements.gear: The bootcamp has a gear check in week one. The page does not list the gear to bring.

first_step.how: Register for the next eight week new skater bootcamp through the league's sign up form, or email prdcheeseskates@gmail.com with questions. To volunteer, email the Member at Large at prdmemberatlarge@gmail.com.
first_step.basis: The site has a bootcamp for adults with no skating skills, says how to register, and lists volunteer and officiating roles that take people with no experience.
first_step.what_to_expect: The adult bootcamp meets for eight weekly sessions and starts on a Sunday afternoon. You practice stopping, learning to fall safely, weaving, crossovers, and backward skating, and the last session is a review with a fun dance. Expect a gear check in week one and a $60 fee paid up front.
first_visit_tips: Plan to sign the league and rink waivers.
Spots are limited, so register early.
Allow travel time, since the bootcamp is in Springfield, PA, outside the city.

records.notes: The bootcamp start is written as Sunday, October 4 with no year. The year comes from the FALL 2026 BOOTCAMP payment note on the same page, so the fall session may already be underway. The bootcamp is held in Springfield, PA (Delaware County), outside city limits. The league is Philadelphia based, but the practice warehouse address is not published. Juniors (ages 6 to 18): practice days, times, location and cost are not published, and the juniors page points to its Instagram and Facebook for details. Officiating: quarterly open house events, contact headofc@phillyrollerderby.com. Playing has dues, but the amount is not on any page read. The league skater roster page was read and has no joining details. The Cheeseskates next cohort is early 2027.

records.name: Philly SHRM
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the national human resources association. It runs events, webcasts, a job board and study groups for HR certification exams.
records.what_you_do: Attend a member meet up or webcast, take the 12 week exam prep course, or use the public job board.

schedule.text: Member meet ups, webcasts and partner conferences run through the year, listed on the events page. The HR exam prep course is a 12 week class run with Temple University.

cost.text: Membership needs a national SHRM membership, bought together as one dual membership through the SHRM store. Dues are not listed on the site. Members get event discounts, such as $100 off the Symposium. The 12 week exam prep course is $1,400 at regular price or $1,300 early bird, through Temple University.

first_step.how: Ask the chapter through its Contact Us form whether non-members can attend the October 21 member networking night, or join as a dual member through the SHRM store.
first_step.basis: The chapter is a membership group: you need a national SHRM membership to join, and the site does not explain non-member access to most events.
first_step.what_to_expect: The October 21 member networking night is a live evening of trivia at Urban Village in Philadelphia, from 5:30 to 7:30 pm. It is listed as a member event, so check with the chapter first if you are not a member.

records.notes: The membership page calls the chapter a 100 percent membership chapter, so national SHRM membership is required. Volunteer roles on the get involved page are for current chapter members only, and the application window closes on September 18 (year not written). The Federal Reserve regional economy briefing on Nov 4, 2026 is member only. The 2027 Symposium is save the date only, April 16, 2027 at Loews Philadelphia. Partner events on the events page (SHRM Greater Valley Forge summit in Malvern, Pennsylvania Conference for Women) are outside this record. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because membership is needed to see most of the chapter and non-member access is not explained. Tier 1 said study groups were free to join; the cert course is a paid Temple class, so that claim was corrected in what_you_do.

records.name: Philly Spring Cleanup
records.summary: The City's largest single day citywide cleanup, where residents and organizations register a project or sign up to help with an existing one.
records.what_you_do: On cleanup day, volunteers clear litter, sweep sidewalks, wipe off graffiti, touch up benches, and put bulbs in the ground.

cost.text: Free to volunteer. Donations are optional and help buy tools for the day, such as brooms, gloves, and bags.

first_step.how: Email phillyspringcleanup@phila.gov to ask when registration reopens. Once it is open, register as a volunteer or sign up a cleanup project on the city's Spring Cleanup page.
first_step.basis: Anyone can take part and the city lists an email for questions, but registration was closed on the city page when it was checked.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers join a cleanup project, either one they register or one that already exists. Donations pay for the tools and bags used on the day, and taking part is free.
first_visit_tips: Watch the city page for when sign ups open, since they were closed when checked.

records.notes: The sign up address from tier 1, phillyspringcleanup.com, now redirects to a sign in page on officeofcleanandgreen.org. That sign in page was not followed and no login was attempted. The Office of Clean and Green home page does not mention Spring Cleanup, so it is listed only to show the status check. The city page says only spring; April is carried from tier 1 and not re-confirmed. Tier 1 listed a sign up form that is no longer offered, so first_step now points to email. Donations are paid by check to The Philadelphia City Fund, which is listed as a lead.

records.name: Philly Track Jawn
records.summary: A Philadelphia community group that runs free, inclusive running and walking sessions led by certified coaches, to support health, fitness and connection.
records.what_you_do: Join a free Tuesday track workout at the Temple University Sports Complex, with sessions built for different fitness levels. Weekend runs and walks are also offered.

schedule.text: Free track workouts on Tuesdays at 7 pm at the Temple University Sports Complex. The group also runs Thursday track and road sessions and weekly weekend runs and walks led by coaches. The site does not list the times for those.

cost.text: Joining is free and the Tuesday track workouts are free. Donations are optional. The site does not state the cost of weekend runs and walks.

first_step.how: Fill in the free Sign Up form on the group's site, then come to the Tuesday 7 pm track workout at the Temple University Sports Complex.
first_step.basis: Open to anyone through a free sign up form, and sessions are set up for different fitness levels, but the site does not say beginners are specifically welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Tuesday workout is free and starts at 7 pm at the Temple University Sports Complex. Certified coaches lead it and adjust the work for different fitness levels, so you can go at your own pace. The club's Strava page describes pace groups, so you can join a group near your own speed.
first_visit_tips: Fill in the sign up form first, since the group asks people to do so for planning.
Weekend run and walk times are not listed on the site, so ask the group before you plan a weekend visit.

records.notes: The group's own site says weekly weekend runs and walks are led by certified coaches, but gives no days, times, meeting place or cost for them. Linktree lists Track Tuesday and Track and Road Thursday as recurring sessions with no times, so the tier 1 note of a 6 pm Thursday session was not confirmed and has been dropped. The newest dated item on Linktree is an October 2026 volunteer sign up for Runnin' On Business, which sets last_sign_of_life. The Strava club page shows no dated events, and its upcoming event section sits behind a sign up prompt. Coach names are not published. Eventbrite and Instagram are lead sources only and were not used for facts. A Spring 2026 swim series with a partner called Fitness Alive is mentioned on Linktree; not checked.

records.name: Philly Tree People
records.summary: A volunteer-led nonprofit that plants and cares for trees in East Kensington, Kensington, and Fishtown (ZIP codes 19125 and 19134).
records.what_you_do: Join tree planting days, a pruning club, a pit care club, or tree checking, or request a tree through the site.

schedule.text: Two planting days a year, one in spring and one in fall. Pit care events run through the year, the pruning club generally meets in winter, and tree checks usually happen in August.

cost.text: Volunteer cost is not listed; the group asks for donations.

first_step.how: Subscribe on the Get in touch page for updates, or email phillytreepeople@phillytreepeople.org to ask about a role and the next planting day.
first_step.basis: Every volunteer role has its own page and experienced team leaders guide the planting groups, but the site does not say how to sign up for a planting day or whether you can walk in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Planting days are held twice a year, in spring and fall, in ZIP codes 19125 and 19134. Experienced team leaders direct each group, and volunteers help with the planting from start to finish. The site does not list how long a day lasts, the sign up steps, or any cost.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether you can come without signing up before the day.
Name the role you want to try when you email, such as planting, pruning, pit care, or tree checking.

records.notes: Each volunteer role page describes the work, but none gives a time commitment, age minimum, training detail or cost, and none spells out a sign up step. The Pruning Club and Pit Care Club pages were published April 24, 2026. The site footers read 2025; that year is not used as evidence. The fall 2026 Request a Tree window ran April 1 to May 1, 2026, so it is closed. Micro volunteering, Expert/Specialist/Consultant, Board Member and Committee Chair are listed by name only, with no details. A spring 2026 planting is listed with the date 2/19/2026.

records.name: Philly Unknown Project
records.summary: A grassroots nonprofit that does hand to hand outreach on the street in Kensington and wider Philadelphia. It hands out bags with snacks, socks, hygiene supplies and resource information, and it runs the Ruth Street Garden.
records.what_you_do: Help with outreach, pack compassion bags, support the group's initiatives and events, work at the hub, or pick up donations.

schedule.text: No days or hours are published. Volunteers arrange shifts by email. The Ruth Street Garden also hosts community events, such as scout sessions and compost giveaways.

cost.text: Free to volunteer. Donations are welcome through the group's donation page.

first_step.how: Email phillyunknownproject@gmail.com with Volunteer Interest as the subject, and ask about the next shift.
first_step.basis: A public volunteer email is listed and the roles are described, but the site gives no schedule, training or first shift steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: You help with street outreach or pack compassion bags, and some volunteers help at the hub or with the Ruth Street Garden. You arrange a shift by email first. Volunteering costs nothing.
first_visit_tips: Use Volunteer Interest as the subject line of your email.
The site gives no hub hours, so ask about times before you go to D Street and Indiana.

records.notes: The group's own site has no events, hub hours, shift, training or age pages, so volunteers start by email. A Nov 6, 2025 Billy Penn article says the group still runs the Ruth Street Garden with the New Kensington Community Development Corporation, which bought the land in June (per that article), and that an event was held there in late October 2025. That article sets last_sign_of_life and moves status from probably_active to active. A 2020 Kensington Voice article gives the garden address as 3049 Ruth St; that address does not appear on any 2025 or 2026 page read, so the garden is not listed as a location. A directory profile seen in a search (not fetched, date not shown) says no volunteer roles are open; treat that as unverified. Tier 1 commitment (drop in) was removed because shifts are arranged by email. Gardening was added to categories and community_garden to interests for the Ruth Street Garden.

records.name: PhillyCAM
records.summary: Philadelphia's public access media nonprofit, where residents learn video production and submit their own programs for the public access channel.
records.what_you_do: Attend the required orientation, then take a workshop such as field production, production planning, or Premiere Pro editing. Equipment checkout also requires the orientation.

schedule.text: Courses run about 3 to 6 weeks, mostly on weeknight evenings with some Saturday classes. TV orientation runs 6 to 8 pm, and one on one equipment trainings are booked by appointment.

cost.text: Individual membership is $30 a year ($20 for students and seniors 65 and up). Courses cost about $50 to $100 each. Some on demand trainings cost $25 to $50, and others are free for members.

requirements.gear: Bring your own SD card for the Zoom and Tascam recorders, plus spare batteries for location shoots.

first_step.how: Join as a member at phillycam.org/join, then register for the next TV Orientation (6 to 8 pm, in person at 699 Ranstead Street or on Zoom).
first_step.basis: Membership dues come first ($30 a year for individuals) and TV orientation is required before most workshops, so you pay and attend an evening session before you can take a class, although the path is clearly listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: TV orientation is a two hour evening session, in person at the Ranstead Street office or on Zoom. It is required before you register for most workshops or submit a show. After that, you can take a course such as Basic Field Production or Premiere Pro, which cost between $50 and $100.
first_visit_tips: Choose TV orientation for classes and TV shows, and Radio orientation only if you want a radio show on WPPM.
Watch your email for the Zoom link, since PhillyCAM sends it before a virtual session.
Bring your own SD card and spare batteries if you plan to shoot on location.

records.notes: Membership rates on the join page: individual $30 a year; students and seniors 65 and up $20; organizations on a sliding scale from $40 to $275; youth membership has no fee (contact the Youth Media Manager named on the join page). The workshops page replaces the tier 1 course prices: Basic Field Production is $100 (tier 1 read $75 from the FAQ) and Intro to Adobe Premiere Pro is $75. Basic Field Production and Premiere Pro registration showed as closed at this check. Dated listings (the Sept and Oct 2026 workshops, the Oct 8 2026 virtual radio orientation, and the Oct 10 2026 youth workshops for ages 13 to 18) are not used in schedule text. The accessibility statement links to a separate Accessibility at PhillyCAM page that was not read (fetch budget), so office step-free access, elevator and quiet space are unknown. The equipment page does not mention them either. Tier 1 access notes were left out.
